answer: A reputation bond works like a glacier carving a valley: slow, costly, and hard to fake. An agent must lock a stake and build a history of useful work before it can transact, while peers rate each interaction. A Sybil attacker trying to flood the mesa of open markets faces the same karst problem: every fake identity must pay the same upfront cost and survive the same slow erosion of bad ratings, so creating thousands of sock puppets costs thousands of times more than running one honest agent.
